payload.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer with $n \\geq 2$. For a sequence $s = (s_1,\\dots,s_{n-1})$ where each $s_i = \\pm 1$, let $f(s)$ be the number of permutations $(a_1,\\dots,a_n)$ of $\\{1,2,\\dots,n\\}$ such that $s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0$ for all $i$. For each $n$, determine the sequences $s$ for which $f(s)$ is maximal.

ambiguities: The phrase determine the sequences s could mean either describe all maximizers or give a representative maximizer; the natural reading is to classify all maximizers
It is not stated whether there may be multiple maximizing sequences, but the optimization is over the full class of sign sequences
The notation a_i is understood as the ith entry of a permutation, not as an arbitrary sequence
implicit_assumptions_surfaced: The sequence s is indexed from 1 to n minus 1
Permutations are being counted in one-line notation as ordered n-tuples
The optimization is over all admissible sign sequences for the fixed n
The function f(s) is finite because only finitely many permutations of {1, 2, ..., n} exist

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is at least 2
s has exactly n minus 1 entries
Each entry s_i is either plus 1 or minus 1
a is a permutation of the set {1, 2, ..., n}
The inequality must hold for every index i from 1 to n minus 1
The expression a_{i+1} minus a_i is compared through strict inequality, so equality is not allowed
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each integer n at least 2, characterize all length n minus 1 sequences of signs plus 1 or minus 1 that maximize the number of permutations of {1, 2, ..., n} whose successive differences have the prescribed signs.
quantifier_order: For each integer n at least 2
For each sign sequence s of length n minus 1 with entries plus 1 or minus 1
Define f(s) as the number of permutations a of {1, 2, ..., n} such that for every i from 1 to n minus 1, s_i times (a_{i+1} minus a_i) is greater than 0
Among all such sequences s for the fixed n, find those that maximize f(s)
